audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for consecration of firstborn, unleavened bread memorial, teaching children, route by wilderness, Joseph's bones, pillar of cloud/fire.

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Consecrate to me every firstborn, opening every womb among children of Israel, among human and among beast; it is mine.

familiar.text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine.

modern.text: “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male. The firstborn from every womb among the Israelites belongs to Me, both of man and beast.”

original.text: קַדֶּשׁ לִ֨י כָל בְּכ֜וֹר פֶּ֤טֶר כָּל רֶ֨חֶם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לִ֖י הֽוּא

verses.restored: Moses said to the people, Remember this day on which you went out from Egypt, from house of servants/slaves, for by strength of hand YHWH brought you out from this; and no leavened bread shall be eaten.

familiar.text: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.

modern.text: So Moses told the people, “Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; for the LORD brought you out of it by the strength of His hand. And nothing leavened shall be eaten.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל הָעָ֗ם זָכ֞וֹר אֶת הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצָאתֶ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִ֧יא יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יֵאָכֵ֖ל חָמֵֽץ

verses.restored: Today you are going out, in month of Aviv.

familiar.text: This day came ye out in the month Abib.

modern.text: Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.

original.text: הַיּ֖וֹם אַתֶּ֣ם יֹצְאִ֑ים בְּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הָאָבִֽיב

verses.restored: And it shall be when YHWH brings you into land of Canaanite, Hittite, Amorite, Hivite, and Jebusite, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall serve this service in this month.

familiar.text: And it shall be when the LORD shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which he sware unto thy fathers to give thee, a land flowing with milk and honey, that thou shalt keep this service in this month.

modern.text: And when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land He swore to your fathers that He would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey—you shall keep this service in this month.

original.text: וְהָיָ֣ה כִֽי יְבִֽיאֲךָ֣ יְהוָ֡ה אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽ֠כְּנַעֲנִי וְהַחִתִּ֨י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֜י וְהַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔ךְ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ וְעָבַדְתָּ֛ אֶת הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on seventh day festival to YHWH.

familiar.text: Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to the LORD.

modern.text: For seven days you are to eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.

original.text: שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תֹּאכַ֣ל מַצֹּ֑ת וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י חַ֖ג לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Unleavened bread shall be eaten seven days; no leavened bread shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you in all your border.

familiar.text: Unleavened bread shall be eaten seven days; and there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.

modern.text: Unleavened bread shall be eaten during those seven days. Nothing leavened may be found among you, nor shall leaven be found anywhere within your borders.

original.text: מַצּוֹת֙ יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְלֹֽא יֵרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֜ חָמֵ֗ץ וְלֹֽא יֵרָאֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ שְׂאֹ֖ר בְּכָל גְּבֻלֶֽךָ

verses.restored: You shall tell your child on that day, saying, It is because of what YHWH did for me when I came out from Egypt.

familiar.text: And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the LORD did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.

modern.text: And on that day you are to explain to your son, ‘This is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’

original.text: וְהִגַּדְתָּ֣ לְבִנְךָ֔ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹ֑ר בַּעֲב֣וּר זֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לִ֔י בְּצֵאתִ֖י מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: It shall be for you as sign upon your hand and as memorial between your eyes, so that Torah/instruction of YHWH may be in your mouth, for with strong hand YHWH brought you out from Egypt.

familiar.text: And it shall be for a sign unto thee upon thine hand, and for a memorial between thine eyes, that the LORD’s law may be in thy mouth: for with a strong hand hath the LORD brought thee out of Egypt.

modern.text: It shall be a sign for you on your hand and a reminder on your forehead that the Law of the LORD is to be on your lips. For with a mighty hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt.

original.text: וְהָיָה֩ לְךָ֨ לְא֜וֹת עַל יָדְךָ֗ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן֙ בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֔יךָ לְמַ֗עַן תִּהְיֶ֛ה תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה בְּפִ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה הוֹצִֽאֲךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: You shall keep this statute at its appointed time from days to days.

familiar.text: Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year.

modern.text: Therefore you shall keep this statute at the appointed time year after year.

original.text: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֛ אֶת הַחֻקָּ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְמוֹעֲדָ֑הּ מִיָּמִ֖ים יָמִֽימָה

verses.restored: And it shall be when YHWH brings you into land of Canaanite, as he swore to you and your fathers, and gives it to you,

familiar.text: And it shall be when the LORD shall bring thee into the land of the Canaanites, as he sware unto thee and to thy fathers, and shall give it thee,

modern.text: And after the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you, as He swore to you and your fathers,

original.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי יְבִֽאֲךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ אֶל אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְךָ֖ וְלַֽאֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָֽךְ

verses.restored: you shall make pass over to YHWH every opener of womb, and every opener of young among beasts that belongs to you; the males are YHWH's.

familiar.text: That thou shalt set apart unto the LORD all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the LORD’s.

modern.text: you are to present to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb. All the firstborn males of your livestock belong to the LORD.

original.text: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ֥ כָל פֶּֽטֶר רֶ֖חֶם לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה וְכָל פֶּ֣טֶר שֶׁ֣גֶר בְּהֵמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: Every firstborn donkey you shall redeem with lamb; and if you do not redeem, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of human among your sons you shall redeem.

familiar.text: And every firstling of an ass thou shalt redeem with a lamb; and if thou wilt not redeem it, then thou shalt break his neck: and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

modern.text: You must redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. And every firstborn of your sons you must redeem.

original.text: וְכָל פֶּ֤טֶר חֲמֹר֙ תִּפְדֶּ֣ה בְשֶׂ֔ה וְאִם לֹ֥א תִפְדֶּ֖ה וַעֲרַפְתּ֑וֹ וְכֹ֨ל בְּכ֥וֹר אָדָ֛ם בְּבָנֶ֖יךָ תִּפְדֶּֽה

verses.restored: And it shall be when your child asks you tomorrow, saying, What is this? you shall say to him, By strength of hand YHWH brought us out from Egypt, from house of servants/slaves.

familiar.text: And it shall be when thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? that thou shalt say unto him, By strength of hand the LORD brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage:

modern.text: In the future, when your son asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you are to tell him, ‘With a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

original.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי יִשְׁאָלְךָ֥ בִנְךָ֛ מָחָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֣ר מַה זֹּ֑את וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֗ד הוֹצִיאָ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים

verses.restored: And it happened, when Pharaoh was hard against sending us, YHWH killed every firstborn in land of Egypt, from firstborn of human to firstborn of beast; therefore I sacrifice to YHWH every opener of womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, that the LORD slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of beast: therefore I sacrifice to the LORD all that openeth the matrix, being males; but all the firstborn of my children I redeem.

modern.text: And when Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both of man and beast. This is why I sacrifice to the LORD the firstborn male of every womb, but I redeem all the firstborn of my sons.’

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי הִקְשָׁ֣ה פַרְעֹה֮ לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג יְהֹוָ֤ה כָּל בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִבְּכֹ֥ר אָדָ֖ם וְעַד בְּכ֣וֹר בְּהֵמָ֑ה עַל כֵּן֩ אֲנִ֨י זֹבֵ֜חַ לַֽיהוָ֗ה כָּל פֶּ֤טֶר רֶ֨חֶם֙ הַזְּכָרִ֔ים וְכָל בְּכ֥וֹר בָּנַ֖י אֶפְדֶּֽה

verses.restored: It shall be as sign upon your hand and as bands between your eyes, for by strength of hand YHWH brought us out from Egypt.

familiar.text: And it shall be for a token upon thine hand, and for frontlets between thine eyes: for by strength of hand the LORD brought us forth out of Egypt.

modern.text: So it shall serve as a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, for with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.” The Pillars of Cloud and Fire

original.text: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאוֹת֙ עַל יָ֣דְכָ֔ה וּלְטוֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִיאָ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: When Pharaoh sent the people, Divine did not lead them by way of land of Philistines, though it was near, for Divine said, Lest the people change mind when they see war and return to Egypt.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:

modern.text: When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, though it was shorter. For God said, “If the people face war, they might change their minds and return to Egypt.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּשַׁלַּ֣ח פַּרְעֹה֮ אֶת הָעָם֒ וְלֹא נָחָ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים דֶּ֚רֶךְ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב ה֑וּא כִּ֣י אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים פֶּֽן יִנָּחֵ֥ם הָעָ֛ם בִּרְאֹתָ֥ם מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה

verses.restored: So Divine turned the people by way of wilderness toward Sea of Reeds; and children of Israel went up armed/arrayed from land of Egypt.

familiar.text: But God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red sea: and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.

modern.text: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. And the Israelites left the land of Egypt arrayed for battle.

original.text: וַיַּסֵּ֨ב אֱלֹהִ֧ים אֶת הָעָ֛ם דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר יַם ס֑וּף וַחֲמֻשִׁ֛ים עָל֥וּ בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם

verses.restored: Moses took bones of Joseph with him, for he had made children of Israel surely swear, saying, Visiting, Divine will visit you, and you shall bring up my bones from this with you.

familiar.text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

modern.text: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him because Joseph had made the sons of Israel swear a solemn oath when he said, “God will surely attend to you, and then you must carry my bones with you from this place.”

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת עַצְמ֥וֹת יוֹסֵ֖ף עִמּ֑וֹ כִּי֩ הַשְׁבֵּ֨עַ הִשְׁבִּ֜יעַ אֶת בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פָּקֹ֨ד יִפְקֹ֤ד אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֧ם אֶת עַצְמֹתַ֛י מִזֶּ֖ה אִתְּכֶֽם

verses.restored: They journeyed from Succoth and camped at Etham, at edge of wilderness.

familiar.text: And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.

modern.text: They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the wilderness.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם בִּקְצֵ֖ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר

verses.restored: YHWH went before them by day in pillar of cloud to guide them by the way, and by night in pillar of fire to give them light, so they could go by day and by night.

familiar.text: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

modern.text: And the LORD went before them in a pillar of cloud to guide their way by day, and in a pillar of fire to give them light by night, so that they could travel by day or night.

original.text: וַֽיהוָ֡ה הֹלֵךְ֩ לִפְנֵיהֶ֨ם יוֹמָ֜ם בְּעַמּ֤וּד עָנָן֙ לַנְחֹתָ֣ם הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְלַ֛יְלָה בְּעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֑ם לָלֶ֖כֶת יוֹמָ֥ם וָלָֽיְלָה

verses.restored: The pillar of cloud by day and pillar of fire by night did not turn aside from before the people.

familiar.text: He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.

modern.text: Neither the pillar of cloud by day nor the pillar of fire by night left its place before the people.

original.text: לֹֽא יָמִ֞ישׁ עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְעַמּ֥וּד הָאֵ֖שׁ לָ֑יְלָה לִפְנֵ֖י הָעָֽם

translation_notes: Firstborn consecration responds to firstborn deliverance/judgment with redemption, not death as ongoing practice.
Unleavened bread is pedagogy: children ask, parents narrate liberation.
Torah/instruction in mouth, hand, and between eyes roots command in embodied memory.
Sea of Reeds is used rather than Red Sea; route avoids immediate war as trauma-aware Divine guidance.
safety_note: Named land peoples require later ethical audit. Firstborn language should emphasize redemption of human firstborn and memory of liberation, not ongoing violence.
